topline.dek: Dave & Buster's just hired a new creative agency with a brief to make 251 locations feel local. Hoka turned New York's five boroughs into rival teams. Outkast and Waffle House turned an Atlanta memory into national news. The brands that play everywhere are paying for the feeling of somewhere. That is our lane. Detroit, Toronto and Atlanta are where we prove it, and national brands are where we take it.

ticker: Dave & Buster's names Gut creative agency of record, brief calls for local relevance at national scale
Kalshi stops using AI-generated people after a creator backlash
Outkast x Waffle House drew a 4 a.m. line in Atlanta
Hoka turned Strava miles into live billboards across New York
Instagram now lets you boost a livestream as it happens
U.S. ban on most Canadian alcohol took effect Sept. 29
31% of Americans now call college very important, a record low
Boston Beer's new CMO starts Oct. 12

hooks.title: Dave & Buster's hired a new creative agency to make a national brand feel local
hooks.what: Dave & Buster's named Gut its creative agency of record, covering brand strategy, creative, social and influencer work, with Mediaplus on media. Both started Oct. 1. The brief calls for connecting nationally scaled campaigns with local relevance and tying local-market activation to brand building. Sales have fallen for 13 straight quarters.
hooks.sowhat: A national brand with 251 locations wrote our pitch into its own brief. An independent creative network beat the incumbent Deloitte Digital to do it.

moves.strategy: This is the brief to keep in our back pocket for national pitches. D&B is betting that local relevance can fix 13 quarters of falling sales, which is the same case we make about our own cities.
moves.data: D&B's quarterly same-store sales. If Gut's first work moves them, we get a public scoreboard for local relevance.
moves.creative: Try writing one D&B idea for Detroit, then see what has to change for it to work in Phoenix. That gap is where the craft is.
moves.production: Sketch what it takes for one shoot to give every market its own cut. Crew, casting, locations and timeline on one page.

hooks.title: Outkast and Waffle House turned a merch drop into a hometown holiday
hooks.what: The collection launched Oct. 2 at the Centennial Olympic Park Waffle House. The first fan showed up around 4 a.m. Outkast has not put out an album since 2006, and 2026 is 30 years of ATLiens.
hooks.sowhat: No new music and no tour, and the line still wrapped the block. Two Atlanta institutions pooled decades of memory, and fans came for the belonging.

moves.strategy: National brands we want to pitch have hometown moments like this in their markets too. Someone should start a list of anniversaries and local institutions by city for our target clients.
moves.data: Search and social volume around Atlanta and ATLiens over the next month. It tells us how long a hometown moment holds attention.
moves.creative: The jacket mattered less than the memory people brought to the line. What would that look like for a brand with 30 years in Detroit?
moves.production: Fans filmed the line themselves and that footage traveled. For drops like this, plan crowd capture and rights on day one.

hooks.title: Kalshi stopped using AI-generated people after a creator caught it copying his video
hooks.what: On Sept. 24, Kalshi said it no longer uses AI-generated content depicting people and is reviewing its agency relationship. Creator Elliot Choy had posted side-by-side stills showing an ad that copied his video and made him look like a white man. A Toronto creator raised a similar complaint in June.
hooks.sowhat: Resemble AI found generative AI in about 9% of ads in Meta's ad library. Licensing an existing creator video typically costs about a quarter of making a new one, so the shortcut was never necessary. Trust is now a production issue.

moves.strategy: Clients are going to ask us about AI and likeness, and we should have an answer before they do. A one-page policy in every scope would help.
moves.data: Resemble AI found generative AI in about 9% of Meta ads. Watch that share, and how often a backlash like this one follows.
moves.creative: Use AI where it helps the craft, like comps, cleanup and versioning. Real people's faces and stories stay real.
moves.production: Keep a paper trail for every asset: where it came from, who owns it and what we licensed. Licensing a creator's video costs about a quarter of making a new one anyway.

hooks.title: The U.S. ban on Canadian booze is turning Ontario's liquor shelf into a pride campaign
hooks.what: A U.S. ban on most bottled Canadian alcohol took effect Sept. 29. Bulk, unbottled spirits can still cross. In LCBO stores, Ontario replaced Buy Canadian messaging with We're All In on Ontario. In July, 9 of 10 provinces agreed to allow direct-to-consumer sales across provincial borders.
hooks.sowhat: Producers lost their biggest export market overnight, and the home market is now being sold on provincial pride. Producers also say the bureaucracy at home is eating the upside.

moves.strategy: If we have spirits or beer clients with Canadian roots, provincial pride just became a shelf strategy. Worth a call before every other brand puts a flag on the label.
moves.data: Sales of Ontario products at the LCBO over the next two quarters, and how the new cross-province direct-to-consumer sales perform.
moves.creative: Ontario pride has its own jokes, places and references. Start there instead of with the maple leaf.
moves.production: Shoot the people and places behind the bottle, with cuts built for in-store screens and social.

hooks.title: AI shopping assistants keep recommending the national chain
hooks.what: A Lightspeed study ran 20,000 shopping prompts and found national chains in 46% to 58% of AI answers. Google AI Overviews recommended no local store 68% of the time. Adding the word independent to a prompt cut chain recommendations from about 44% to as low as 9%.
hooks.sowhat: More than half of North American shoppers have used AI to shop, and nearly three quarters of under-35s have. If a brand is hard for the machine to read, it never makes the list.

moves.strategy: We could sell an AI shelf audit tomorrow. Ask the assistants what shoppers ask, write down who shows up and walk the client through the gaps.
moves.data: Lightspeed found chains in 46% to 58% of AI answers. Run the same prompts for our clients every month so we can show movement.
moves.creative: Copy has to work twice now, once for the machine reading it and once for the person repeating it. Write product pages that do both.
moves.production: Ship a content kit with the hero work: specs, FAQs, reviews and clean product photos that assistants can pull from.

hooks.title: Toyota is marketing to the AI before the buyer
hooks.what: Automotive News reports Toyota is moving from search engine optimization to generative engine optimization because AI agents are replacing search for early vehicle research. The same week, Toyota opened a $50 million battery research center near Saline, Michigan.
hooks.sowhat: The first conversation about a car now happens in a chat window. Whoever shapes that answer shapes the shortlist, long before a dealer gets the lead.

moves.strategy: Every auto and dealer conversation should cover where buyers do their early research now. Toyota already treats an AI answer as the first test drive.
moves.data: Ask the major assistants about a client's best-selling model each month and log what they say. That log becomes our baseline.
moves.creative: Vague taglines vanish in an AI summary. Specific claims about range, price and features are the ones that get quoted.
moves.production: Model walkarounds and spec videos are reference content now. Plan them as a library, with transcripts.

hooks.title: Only 31% of Americans now call college very important
hooks.what: Gallup's August poll found 31% rate a college education very important, down from 70% in 2013. Among Black adults the number fell from 65% in 2019 to 40%. Only 12% call a four-year degree affordable, per Lumina and Gallup.
hooks.sowhat: Schools can no longer assume people value a degree. Every enrollment message now has to prove the payoff in plain terms.
hooks.counter: Fairly important rose to 39%, so most people still see some value.

moves.strategy: Education clients can't assume people value a degree anymore. Lead with outcomes and with what it costs to say yes.
moves.data: Among Black adults, the share calling college very important fell from 65% to 40% in six years. That gap matters most for the schools in our cities.
moves.creative: Cast real graduates and let them talk about money and work the way they would with a friend.
moves.production: A documentary alumni series, shot once and cut by program and audience.

hooks.title: Taco Bell and Duolingo take Taco Day global
hooks.what: On Oct. 6, Taco Bell and Duolingo will celebrate Global Taco Day with a Duo Habanero Sauce whose packets carry taco wisdom in nine languages. The sauce comes free with a Doritos Locos Tacos order. Duo may appear in Toronto, Mumbai and Shanghai, and there is a New York restaurant takeover.
hooks.sowhat: Two brands whose personality fans already know are borrowing each other's audiences. Diners are cutting back, so the deal is built to cost them nothing.

moves.strategy: Read this as an audience swap. Taco Bell gets Duolingo's fans and the diner pays nothing extra, which is why it works while people cut back.
moves.data: How much of the conversation happens outside the U.S. It's a live test of whether a collab travels.
moves.creative: Duo on a sauce packet lands in one look. When we brief a collab, the first test is whether it reads in a second.
moves.production: The packaging is the media here, in nine languages and small runs. Production should be in the room when packaging gets designed.

hooks.title: The High Museum turns 100 with a free block party and a Braves hat
hooks.what: The High was founded in October 1926. For its centennial it is reinstalling the collection with more than 70 quilts by African American artists, alongside LGBTQ+ photography and Nigerian modernism. Free events include a UPS Second Sunday on Oct. 11, where a Braves High 100 hat debuts, and a block party on Oct. 18.
hooks.sowhat: A museum is acting like a city brand, with free access, a sports collab and food partners. This anniversary is built for the whole city, not just its members.

moves.strategy: Anniversaries can be civic platforms with sports, food and retail partners. Bring this to arts and city clients as a model.
moves.data: Attendance at the free days compared with a normal Sunday. That number shows whether free access actually grows the audience.
moves.creative: The Braves hat will travel farther than any poster. Ask what people in the city would actually wear.
moves.production: A block party is a production, with permits, capture and partner content. Plan it like a shoot.

hooks.title: A Detroit soup kitchen is becoming a sit-down restaurant
hooks.what: Capuchin Soup Kitchen and Massimo Bottura's Food for Soul are turning the Meldrum center on Detroit's east side into Refettorio Detroit. The $2.4 million renovation will serve 200 to 250 guests a day, with a starter, entrée, dessert and coffee brought to the table. Construction is slated to finish in January 2027.
hooks.sowhat: Treating people with dignity becomes the design brief. That standard of hospitality is something food brands and civic partners can learn from.

moves.strategy: This is a model of hospitality as respect, and food and civic partners will want to hear about it.
moves.data: Meals served per day once it opens, against the target of 200 to 250. It's a simple way to tell the story.
moves.creative: Tell it through the meal itself: the plates, the service, coffee brought to the table. The details carry the dignity.
moves.production: Construction runs until January 2027. Documenting the build would give a partner a year of content.

hooks.title: Value fashion is getting squeezed out of the Southeast
hooks.what: Cato is closing 120 stores by year end, more than 10% of its fleet, and its biggest market is the Southeast. In metro Atlanta, Belk will close its store at The Forum Peachtree Corners on Jan. 15 after about 25 years. Atlanta Apparel runs Oct. 6 to 9.
hooks.sowhat: Shoppers on a budget still want style. The stores built for them are disappearing, and off-price chains and online resale are taking their place.

moves.strategy: Somebody should find out where Southeast value shoppers go when their store closes. A retailer or mall operator would pay for that research.
moves.data: Store closures across value chains in the Southeast, and foot traffic at the off-price stores nearby.
moves.creative: Style on a budget is a real brief. The work can look good without pretending to be luxury.
moves.production: Creator try-ons and hauls reach this shopper better than a big studio shoot.

hooks.title: GLP-1 use is up to 18% of adults, and snacks are answering with protein
hooks.what: FTI Consulting puts GLP-1 use at about 18% of U.S. adults, up from 14%, and 23% among ages 35 to 54. Users are cutting chips, sweets, soft drinks and alcohol. Cheez-It Protein launches this month with 7 grams per serving.
hooks.sowhat: Once a heritage cracker has a protein line, protein no longer sets anyone apart. The next edge is satiety, portion size and fitting a smaller appetite.

moves.strategy: Before a CPG client launches another protein line, show them their portfolio from inside a GLP-1 household.
moves.data: FTI puts use at 23% for ages 35 to 54. Watch basket data for chips, sweets and soft drinks in that group.
moves.creative: People on GLP-1s care about feeling full. Talk about that, and treat smaller packs as a good thing.
moves.production: Big hero servings look wrong to this shopper. Reshoot portion and pack visuals.

hooks.title: Discount is the growth format in grocery
hooks.what: Metro is converting its West Queen West store in Toronto into a Food Basics, one of 10 Ontario conversions it announced. In the U.S., Gen Z and millennials drove 81% of private label spending gains in the year to June 14, per Circana data via Spins.
hooks.sowhat: Younger shoppers see store brands and discount banners as the smart choice. Every dry goods brand is now competing with the retailer's own label for trust.

moves.strategy: Find the moment young shoppers pick the store brand and what would bring them back. That's a shop-along study we could run in any market.
moves.data: Circana says Gen Z and millennials drove 81% of private label gains. Watch whether that holds as discount banners keep growing.
moves.creative: Name brands need a reason beyond price. Taste, ritual and pride are good places to start.
moves.production: As discount banners grow, shelf and in-store content does more of the selling. Budget for it.

hooks.title: The Outset is closing, and celebrity skincare keeps losing altitude
hooks.what: Scarlett Johansson's skincare brand is shutting down after about four years. In the same week, Rhode expanded to more than 500 Sephora stores across 19 European countries, and Cakes Body passed $100 million in sales in three years.
hooks.sowhat: A famous name gets you in the door but doesn't keep you there. The brands still growing have one hero product, a community that talks for them and serious distribution.

moves.strategy: Use this week as the example in beauty pitches. Rhode and Cakes Body are growing on community and distribution while a famous founder's brand closes.
moves.data: Repeat purchase and community share of voice say more about a beauty brand's future than follower counts.
moves.creative: Let customers be the faces and keep the founder as one voice among many.
moves.production: Put budget into an always-on creator program ahead of a single hero shoot.

charts.name: Hometown pride as strategy
charts.evidence: Outkast x Waffle House, Ontario's Buy Ontario push and the High's centennial all landed the same week.
charts.counter: It is three examples in one week. It needs more weeks before it counts as a pattern.
charts.move: Map local institutions and anniversaries for each city client.

charts.name: Buy local, backed by policy
charts.evidence: The U.S. ban took effect Sept. 29, and LCBO stores now push We're All In on Ontario.
charts.counter: Producers say red tape at home erases much of the gain.
charts.move: Help Canadian spirits and beer brands tell a provincial story.

charts.name: AI answers as the shelf
charts.evidence: National chains appeared in 46% to 58% of AI shopping answers, and Toyota is optimizing for AI agents.
charts.counter: AI referrals are still a small share of total traffic, and measurement is early.
charts.move: Lead with an AI shelf audit as an entry project.

charts.name: Generative engine optimization in auto
charts.evidence: Toyota is shifting budget from SEO to GEO for early vehicle research.
charts.counter: One automaker has made the move public. Others may be quieter or slower.
charts.move: Bring a GEO point of view to Detroit auto conversations now.

charts.name: Americans drinking less
charts.evidence: Boston Beer's advertising, promotion and selling costs rose 16.4% in Q2, and both Boston Beer and Athletic Brewing changed CMOs in September.
charts.counter: Global beer volume is still forecast to grow about 1.5%, driven by emerging markets.
charts.move: Sell moderation and occasion-based work to beer and spirits clients.

charts.name: Artist-edition packaging
charts.evidence: Absolut's 2026 Artist Edition with KAWS launched Oct. 1.
charts.counter: Absolut has done artist editions for decades, so this is a format coming back, not a new one.
charts.move: Pair packaging with a local artist for more credibility than a famous one brings.

charts.name: GLP-1 households
charts.evidence: About 18% of U.S. adults now use a GLP-1.
charts.counter: Cost and coverage shifts could slow adoption.
charts.move: Plan for smaller baskets in snack, bev and QSR.

charts.name: Protein in everything
charts.counter: Demand is real. Most consumers say they want more protein.
charts.move: Shift the claim from grams to satiety and portion.

charts.name: Discount grocery formats
charts.evidence: Metro is converting 10 Ontario stores to Food Basics.
charts.counter: A strike weighed on Metro's results, so some of this is cost cutting.
charts.move: Give challenger brands the trust cues that discount banners lack.

charts.name: Diners trading down
charts.evidence: Diners spend about $100 a week eating out, $15 less than in June 2025. 52% now order water instead of a paid drink.
charts.counter: Weekly spend has ticked back up from earlier this year.
charts.move: Keep value obvious on the menu, with photos and clear deals.

charts.name: Brand collabs with app mascots
charts.evidence: Taco Bell x Duolingo for Global Taco Day.
charts.counter: Duo shows up everywhere, which can wear thin.
charts.move: Choose partners for audience overlap, not for noise.

charts.name: Dirty soda and drink customization
charts.evidence: Swig opened in Brookhaven and won't sign an exclusive deal with Coke.
charts.counter: Utah-born chains do not always travel well. Watch the second-year numbers.
charts.move: For bev clients, look at customization as a ritual, not a menu item.

charts.name: Value fashion squeeze
charts.evidence: Cato is closing 120 stores, and Belk is closing a 25-year anchor in Peachtree Corners.
charts.counter: Off-price chains like TJ Maxx keep growing, so the money is moving, not leaving.
charts.move: Follow where the budget-conscious shopper goes next.

charts.name: Team x artist merch
charts.evidence: The Pistons and Big Sean launched Creatives Across Continents, a collection built from submissions by creatives worldwide.
charts.counter: The launch date has not been confirmed, so watch execution.
charts.move: Use the open-call model for brands that want creative credibility.

charts.name: Museums as city platforms
charts.evidence: The High's centennial includes free days and a Braves hat. The DIA's reimagined African American art galleries are on view.
charts.counter: Anniversaries end. The question is what lasts after the party.
charts.move: Help arts clients build year-round partner programs.

charts.name: Doubt about the value of college
charts.evidence: Only 31% call college very important, down from 70% in 2013.
charts.move: Lead with outcomes and lower the perceived risk of enrolling.

charts.name: Celebrity skincare
charts.evidence: The Outset is closing after about four years.
charts.counter: Rhode keeps scaling, so the problem is the operator, not the fame.
charts.move: Put product and community first, and use fame as an accelerant.

charts.name: Superstar festival returns
charts.evidence: Hits Daily Double reports Drake is in the conversation to headline Coachella 2027.
charts.counter: This is a rumor. Nothing is confirmed.
charts.move: Watch it, but don't plan around it.

bsides.title: One word changes what AI recommends
bsides.why: Adding independent to a shopping prompt cut chain recommendations from about 44% to as low as 9%.
bsides.watch: Local business groups teaching shoppers how to prompt, and brands writing for those prompts.

bsides.title: Dignity as a service model
bsides.why: Refettorio Detroit replaces the cafeteria line with seated, three-course service.
bsides.watch: Food brands and chefs signing on as guest partners in 2027.

bsides.title: Open-call merch collections
bsides.why: The Pistons and Big Sean invited designers worldwide to answer one creative prompt for a retail collection.
bsides.watch: Other teams and artists borrowing the model.

bsides.title: Fragrance prep for the skin
bsides.why: Obart and Future Society are building primers that make fragrance last longer.
bsides.watch: A dedicated fragrance prep shelf at Sephora or Ulta.

dropping.title: A celebrity name as the whole strategy
dropping.evidence: The Outset closed after four years despite strong positioning.
dropping.counter: Founder-operated brands like Rhode still scale.
dropping.instead: One hero product, a real community and serious distribution.

dropping.title: Protein as the headline claim
dropping.evidence: Cheez-It has a protein line now, and reviewers call the trend overrated.
dropping.counter: Demand for protein is still real.

dropping.title: Mid-tier department store anchors
dropping.evidence: Belk's Peachtree Corners store closes Jan. 15 after 25 years, and The Forum is betting on a facelift.
dropping.counter: Some anchors are being replaced by experiential tenants, not left empty.

headphones.title: What shaped the sound of Detroit techno?
headphones.why: Carl Craig on how Electrifying Mojo's radio show tied a generation together. A great reference for Detroit music and brand work.

headphones.title: Toyota's September surge; AI and the retail customer journey
headphones.why: The SEO to GEO shift explained from inside auto.

headphones.title: Fans line up at Waffle House for limited Outkast merch
headphones.why: Two minutes of what fandom looks like in person. Worth showing in a pitch.

headphones.title: Inside the enrollment cliff hitting U.S. colleges
headphones.why: Pairs with the Gallup data for any education conversation.

headphones.title: 431. Koen Pauwels on word of mouth
headphones.why: Research-backed look at what makes people talk about a brand. Good for the Hook conversation.

headphones.title: Brand strategy has completely changed in 2026
headphones.why: Long, but useful for the strategy team's own thinking.

headphones.title: Oct. 2 headlines
headphones.why: Wayne County backs Google data center plans, and Reclaim the Rivers budgets $90 million. A fast local scan.

headphones.title: Why so many plan to leave Toronto
headphones.why: Polling on people planning to move away within five years. Context for any Toronto retail or civic brief.

headphones.title: #1445 The hot new journalist who was actually AI
headphones.why: Interesting media story, but not tied to a vertical this week.

headphones.title: Diner en Blanc Detroit 2026, official video
headphones.why: A pretty event recap with nothing new to learn.

spirits.pov: With Americans drinking less, the brands that win sell the occasion and the place, not the proof. In Canada, provincial pride now comes with shelf space.
spirits.opener: What occasion do you own when people drink less but better?
spirits.research: Moderation occasions by city: who is still drinking, when, and with whom.
spirits.creative: Show what a better night looks like for someone drinking less.
spirits.production: Maker films and place-led photos, cut for shelf screens and social.

education.pov: Only 31% call college very important. Enrollment marketing has to prove the payoff in plain language.
education.opener: What does a graduate's first two years actually look like, in their words?
education.research: Outcome storytelling: which kinds of proof move first-generation and Black families.
education.creative: Real graduates talking about money, work and what changed for them.
education.production: One documentary alumni shoot, cut by program.

cpg.pov: Protein claims are table stakes. The next edge is satiety and portion for GLP-1 households.
cpg.opener: How does your shelf look to a household where one person is on a GLP-1?
cpg.research: Basket studies of GLP-1 households in Detroit, Toronto and Atlanta.
cpg.creative: Talk about feeling full, and make the smaller pack the hero.
cpg.production: New portion and pack photography for smaller appetites.

drygoods.pov: Young shoppers trust store brands and discount banners. Name brands have to earn that trust back.
drygoods.opener: Why would a 27-year-old pay more for you than for the store brand?
drygoods.research: The moment of choice: shop-alongs at discount and conventional banners.
drygoods.creative: Give people a reason to pick the name brand that has nothing to do with price.
drygoods.production: Shelf and in-store content kits built for discount banners.

beauty.pov: Fame opens the door and community keeps it open. The Outset closing while Rhode scales says it all.
beauty.opener: If your founder went quiet for six months, who keeps talking about you?
beauty.research: Which community behaviors predict repeat purchase.
beauty.creative: Customers as the faces, with the founder as one voice.
beauty.production: An always-on creator program in place of one hero shoot.

music.pov: Heritage and place pull harder than novelty. Outkast drew a 4 a.m. line with no new album.
music.opener: Which anniversary in the catalog belongs to a city?
music.research: Fan attachment to place across legacy catalogs in all three cities.
music.creative: Find the anniversary that belongs to a city and tell it through the fans.
music.production: Live sessions planned to be boosted on Instagram while they happen.

foodbev.pov: Hospitality is a brand signal. Refettorio Detroit and Swig both win by how the experience feels.
foodbev.opener: What does your brand feel like at the table, not on the shelf?
foodbev.research: Ritual mapping: when customization and hospitality turn into habit.
foodbev.creative: Show what it feels like to sit at the table.
foodbev.production: Document a build or a ritual over several months.

qsr.pov: Diners are cutting $15 a week. Collabs that cost them nothing and make them laugh still win.
qsr.opener: Whose fans would get your joke on the first try?
qsr.research: Value perception by daypart and city.
qsr.creative: A collab whose joke reads in one look and costs the diner nothing.
qsr.production: Packaging as media, in small runs.

fashion.pov: Value fashion is losing stores, but its shoppers still want style. The money is moving, not leaving.
fashion.opener: Where does your customer shop now that her store closed?
fashion.research: Southeast value shopper study: off-price, resale and social commerce.
fashion.creative: Style on a budget that still looks good.

arts.pov: Museums are acting like city brands. The High's 100th is built for the whole city, with a Braves hat to prove it.
arts.opener: Who in this city should feel like the museum is theirs, and doesn't yet?
arts.research: Belonging and access barriers by neighborhood.
arts.creative: Make something people in the city would wear or carry.
arts.production: Capture plans for free days and block parties.

auto.pov: The first test drive now happens in a chat window. Toyota is already optimizing for it.
auto.opener: What does ChatGPT say about your best-selling model right now?
auto.research: GEO audit across assistants, plus buyer interviews on how they research.
auto.creative: Specific claims an AI would quote back.
auto.production: A library of model walkarounds and spec videos.

retail.pov: AI recommends the national chain about half the time. Local brands have to be legible to machines and proud in person.
retail.opener: When someone asks an AI for your category in your city, who shows up?
retail.research: AI shelf audit across 20 prompts per client category.
retail.creative: Copy that machines can read and people repeat.
retail.production: Structured content kits that ship with the hero assets.

calendar.title: High Museum Second Sunday
calendar.note: Free. The Braves High 100 hat debuts.

calendar.title: Halloween on a Saturday
calendar.note: A full weekend for candy and costumes.

reel.title: Hoka turned Strava miles into live billboards
reel.what: A month-long challenge pitted New York's five boroughs against each other on one leaderboard. Strava data refreshed weekly on screens in Times Square, Tribeca, SoHo and Williamsburg. Six creators repped the boroughs, and a block party on Oct. 3 closed it out.
reel.steal: A full loop with no hero film: owned data, a participation mechanic, refreshable media and a physical finale.

reel.title: KFC turned its platform into a game show
reel.what: Don't Crack is a game show built on the three-year-old Believe in Chicken platform, with 30 fans competing for a $67,000 prize.
reel.steal: A platform that keeps producing new formats is worth more than one big spot.

reel.title: On cast Zendaya as an action hero
reel.what: On's latest push casts Zendaya as an action star, aimed at younger women.
reel.steal: Cast against the category's usual look and the audience notices.

reel.title: Chili's made merch about the suburbs
reel.what: Chili's released an apparel collection inspired by the suburbs.
reel.steal: Merch that laughs with the brand's own audience gets worn.

reel.title: Beekeeper's Naturals mixed hand-drawn art with AI
reel.what: Hand-drawn illustration, AI and compositing bring real customer stories to life.
reel.steal: AI works best as one layer in a handmade process, not as the whole process.

reel.title: Instagram lets you boost a livestream while it's live
reel.what: The live video itself becomes the ad across Feed, Stories and Reels, and runs only while the stream is on. Instagram recommends scheduling at least two hours ahead.
reel.steal: Listening parties, studio sessions and launches can now be paid media without a full campaign setup.

reel.title: A creator-director joins a commercial roster
reel.what: Sibling Rivalry signed Chicago-based Gracie Koh, known online as @gkohfilms, for commercial-grade craft with social fluency.
reel.steal: Creator-directors are now on production rosters. Build them into treatments early.

reel.title: Production models are shifting
reel.what: MADRE added Obsidian as Midwest representation, and Tinderflint went rosterless, dropping the traditional production-company model.
reel.steal: There are new ways to staff a shoot. Midwest representation matters for Detroit-based production.

reel.title: Local, handmade type is having a moment
reel.what: Figuree lists vernacular, locally specific references and imperfect lettering among late-2026 type directions. Canva saw DIY and scrapbook searches rise 90% year over year. Rapha's refresh built six typefaces from its own archive.
reel.steal: Pull type and texture from a place's own signs and archives. That is specificity you can see.

motion.what: Gut is creative agency of record and Mediaplus handles media, both from Oct. 1. CMO Jeremy Tucker joined in June from AutoNation.
motion.door: The brief asks for national campaigns with local relevance. Watch for project work around local activation.

motion.what: Allison Stransky, from Samsung, starts as CMO on Oct. 12. Advertising, promotion and selling costs rose 16.4% in Q2.
motion.door: A new CMO is a natural moment to introduce ourselves with a point of view on drinking less.

motion.what: The nonalcoholic brewer changed CMOs in September as Americans drink less.
motion.door: Nonalcoholic beer needs occasions and culture, which is our strength.

motion.what: Publicis won PepsiCo's global media and pulled out of Coca-Cola's global media pitch.
motion.door: Media is consolidating at the holding companies. Cultural and creative project work sits outside those deals, so watch for it.

motion.what: Parent company Deckers passed $1 billion in quarterly revenue, and Hoka sales rose close to 8%. It is chasing younger buyers with creators and community formats.
motion.door: Community-led formats in cities are exactly what we build.

motion.what: Toyota is moving budget from SEO to GEO for early vehicle research.
motion.door: A GEO content and production offer for auto, starting with the brands next door.
